SMTO-API-0005 — A request to SMTO was missing details or in the wrong form

GUID: f6c8b053-18ab-4af4-936c-c68e3055773b
Slug: api-request-invalid
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO or a Gateway received a request it couldn't read, so it turned it down. This can come from an out-of-date page, SMTO and a Gateway being on different versions, or a typed terminal command.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read What the server reported and any Fields to correct in this panel, fix the listed values, and send again. Those lines name exactly which detail SMTO couldn't accept.
  2. Reload this page, check whether your change is already there, and repeat the action only if it isn't. A page left open across an SMTO update can send requests in an older form that SMTO no longer reads.
  3. If it happened while a task used a Gateway, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates. A Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) on a different version may not recognize SMTO's request.
  4. If you ran aor run in a terminal, make sure --input holds one set of named values in curly braces, or use --prompt with plain text instead. The command refuses an --input value that isn't a single named set of values.

What success looks like

  • The action completes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which page or command you used. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it will be turned down the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A request failed input validation at an SMTO or Gateway endpoint (for example CLI --input not decoding to a JSON object, a Gateway operation route answering 'Invalid execution request.', or an otherwise unclassified HTTP 400).

What this means

  • CLI JSON input is not an object, a private Gateway route fails request-model validation, or an unclassified HTTP 400 falls back to this request category. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • CLI JSON input is not an object, a private Gateway route fails request-model validation, or an unclassified HTTP 400 falls back to this request category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the route and named validation fields while keeping private body values out of diagnostics.

How to fix it

  • Check the reported field issues and endpoint in Technical details. For the CLI, pass --input as a JSON object such as '{"task": "list files"}' or use --prompt; for Gateway operation routes (validation details are deliberately withheld), compare the Server and Gateway versions and update the mismatched component; reload stale browser pages.
  • Correct the named input fields using their documented types and constraints.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported request validates at the intended API boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
